Module org.egothor.radixor
Package org.egothor.stemmer.trie

Class CompiledNode<V>

java.lang.Object
org.egothor.stemmer.trie.CompiledNode<V>
Type Parameters:
V - value type
public final class CompiledNode<V> extends Object
Immutable compiled trie node optimized for read access.

The returned arrays are the internal backing storage of the compiled node. They are exposed for efficient access by closely related trie infrastructure and therefore must never be modified by callers. The node itself is still immutable from the public API perspective because construction wires these arrays once and all lookup operations thereafter treat them as read-only.

    • CompiledNode

      public CompiledNode(char[] edgeLabels, CompiledNode<V>[] children, V[] orderedValues, int maxExpandedIndex, int... orderedCounts)
      Creates one validated compiled node.
      Parameters:
      maxExpandedIndex - upper bound for the dense lookup interval size; zero disables dense lookup. Larger values improve direct-index likelihood while increasing dense table memory in compact-label nodes.
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if any array argument is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if the edge-related arrays or value-related arrays do not have matching lengths or the dense interval size is negative

    • CompiledNode

      public CompiledNode(char[] edgeLabels, CompiledNode<V>[] children, V[] orderedValues, boolean acceptsRemainingInput, int maxExpandedIndex, int... orderedCounts)
      Creates one validated compiled node.
      Parameters:
      acceptsRemainingInput - whether this node accepts any remaining lookup input
      maxExpandedIndex - upper bound for the dense lookup interval size
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if any array argument is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if the edge-related arrays or value-related arrays do not have matching lengths, the dense interval size is negative, or an accepting node has children

    • findChild

      public CompiledNode<V> findChild(char edge)
      Finds a child for the supplied edge character. Lookup order is:
      1. dense array index (if the label interval is compact enough),
      2. small-child linear scan when the fallback node has 4 or fewer edges,
      3. binary search over sorted labels.
      Parameters:
      edge - edge character
      Returns:
      child node, or null if absent
